title: Annotatio IV §.XXIII open: Reformed constant — same emptied/exalted body as to first communicants; Wren — stop mid-XXIII
pass_a_gloss: §. XXIII. Therefore the Reformed’s constant sentence of mind is that Christ’s true and substantial body, which once on earth was emptied, but now in heaven is exalted, is present in the Sacred Supper to modern Communicants always and until Christ is to return to judge the living and the dead, under that quality and in that mode under which quality or in which mode it was present to the first Communicants in the very Sacred use of the Supper: For it is no less obvious to the Reformed Faith that Christ’s crucified body, inasmuch as it is crucified, is present in the Supper (SPIRITUALLY namely) than it remains persuaded to the Lutheran Faith that Christ’s glorified body, and therefore Spiritual inasmuch as such, is yet eaten with the mouth of the body. But to one disputing and arguing either that to be present in the thing itself and to be present Spiritually fight each other, or that a spiritual mode of being present does not fit a body, we cannot but recite what Matthew Wren the Englishman answers most sharply to the Racovian Catechism inferring by a like pact… To the FORMER indeed: Do you say truly, he says, that in the thing itself and spiritually fight? Is the spiritual condition so hostile that it devours the Real?… For the more spiritual a thing is, the more it can be discerned to be…
pass_b_english: §.XXIII: Reformed constant mind — the true substantial body once emptied on earth, now exalted in heaven, is present to modern communicants in the same quality/mode as to the first communicants, until the judgment return.

Crucified-as-crucified present SPIRITUALLY is as obvious to them as glorified-body oral eating is to Lutherans. Wren vs Racovian: ‘really’ and ‘spiritually’ do not fight — the more spiritual, the more a thing is. Stop mid-XXIII (Wren’s second reply remains).
source_text: §. XXIII. Itaque Reformatorum constans animi sententia est, verum & substantiale corpus Christi, quod olim in terris fuit exinanitum, nunc verò in cœlis exaltatum, sub ea qualitate, eóque modô, Communicantibus modernis semper & usquedum Christus rediturus est ad judicandum vivos & mortuos, in Cœna S. adesse, sub qua qualitate quóve modô primis Communicantibus, in ipso Sacro Cœnæ usu, præsens fuit: Neque enim minùs Reformatorum Fidei obvium est, corpus Christi crucifixum, quatenus crucifixum est, (SPIRITUALITER scil.) in Cœna præsens esse, quàm Lutheranæ Fidei adhuc persuasum manet, glorificatum corpus Christi, eóque Spirituale, quatenus tale, ore tamen corporis, manducari. Disputanti autem atque arguenti: vel, re ipsa præsens esse, & Spiritualiter adesse, pugnare inter se; vel, spiritualem adessendi modum, in corpus non competere, non possumus non recitare, quæ admodùm acutè Catechesi Racoviensi, simili pactô inferenti, Mattheus Wren Anglus respondet… AD PRIUS quidem: Ain verò Tu, inquit, re ipsa, atque spiritualiter, pugnare? tam infensa est spiritualis conditio, ut Realem devoret?… Etenim, quò magis spirituale quid est, eò magis esse id, dignosci potest…
